playschool.tagline: Where the first school day feels like home
playschool.about: We are a play school and daycare for children from 1 year 8 months to 5½ years, in a ground-floor bungalow with its own garden on Shastri Nagar Road, two lanes behind the Civil Hospital. Children come to us for Play Group, Nursery, LKG and UKG, and working parents leave their little ones with us till 6 in the evening in our daycare. Every class has one teacher and one didi for at most 15 children, so a shy child, a child who still wears a diaper, or a child who speaks only Marwari at home is seen and settled, not lost in a crowd. The whole day is built around play — rhymes, blocks, sand, water, colour, stories and the garden — and the letters and numbers arrive gently, in UKG, when the hands and the mind are ready. Parents get a photo and a two-line note on WhatsApp every afternoon, and the gate, the garden and every room are on CCTV that the owner watches from the office.

products.name: Play Group (1 yr 8 m – 2½ yrs)
products.desc: A two-hour morning for the littlest ones — a parent or grandparent may sit in the first week. Free play, rhymes with actions, sand and water trays, finger painting and a snack together at the small table.
features: Only 12 children, 1 teacher + 1 didi
Parent can stay for the first 5 days
Diaper-friendly, with a changing room
No books, no bag — just play and songs

products.name: Nursery (2½ – 3½ yrs)
products.desc: Three hours a day of play-based learning — colours, shapes, big and small, animals and fruits through blocks, puzzles, clay and picture books. Toilet training is handled calmly by the class didi.
features: Maximum 15 children per class
Toilet training with the didi, no scolding
Weekly theme: farm, rain, my family, Diwali
Hindi and English rhymes, both every day

products.name: LKG (3½ – 4½ yrs)
products.desc: Pre-writing without pressure — tracing in sand, crayons and dot-to-dot before any pencil, letter sounds through songs, counting with real things like pebbles and spoons, and a story every single day.
features: Phonics sounds, not rote A-B-C
Counting 1 to 20 with objects
One art, one music, one PT period daily
Two workbooks for the whole year

products.name: UKG (4½ – 5½ yrs)
products.desc: Reading three-letter words, writing own name, numbers to 100, simple addition with beads, and the confidence to speak in front of the class — so the move to Class 1 in any CBSE or state-board school is smooth.
features: Reading readiness in English and Hindi
Show-and-tell every Friday
Class 1 interview practice in February
Progress book shared every quarter

Pick-up by registered persons only

services.name: Admission guidance
services.desc: Tell us the child's date of birth and we will tell you the right class, the documents, the fee and the next intake, and show you around with your child.

offer.title: Early-Bird Admission for the April Session
offer.text: Register before 28 February and the ₹3,000 admission fee is waived, with the admission kit at ₹2,999 instead of ₹3,499 — for all four classes.

reviews.name: Neha T., mother of a Nursery child
reviews.text: My son cried at two other schools and we had given up. Here the teacher let me sit in the classroom for the first week and the didi, Sunita, learnt the words he uses at home. By the second week he was running in on his own. The 2 pm photo on WhatsApp is the highlight of my working day.

reviews.name: Rajesh & Pooja, both working parents
reviews.text: We needed daycare till 6 and were scared of leaving a two-and-a-half-year-old that long. The same two didis are with the children every day, the nap mattresses are clean, and when our daughter had a fever the owner called us herself within ten minutes. The only thing we would like is a Saturday option every week, not just on request.

reviews.name: Dr. Meenakshi R., mother of a UKG child
reviews.text: As a paediatrician I looked at the toilets, the drinking water and the hand-washing routine before anything else, and they passed. My daughter learnt to read three-letter words through phonics, not by memorising, and she got into Class 1 at the school we wanted without any coaching.

faq.q: From what age do you take children, and which class will my child go to?
faq.a: We take children from 1 year 8 months. Play Group is up to 2½ years, Nursery 2½ to 3½, LKG 3½ to 4½ and UKG 4½ to 5½, with the age counted on 31 March of the admission year. Send us the date of birth on WhatsApp and we will tell you the class and whether a seat is open.

faq.q: What are the timings, and is there daycare?
faq.a: Play Group runs 9:30 to 11:30 am, Nursery 9 am to 12 noon, LKG till 12:30 and UKG till 1 pm, Monday to Friday. Daycare continues after class till 3 pm (half day) or 6 pm (full day) with lunch, nap and snack. Saturday care is available on request at ₹250 a day; Sunday we are closed.

faq.q: How do you keep the children safe?
faq.a: One teacher and one didi stay with at most 15 children, the gate is locked during school hours with a guard, and every room, the garden and the gate are on CCTV watched from the office. Children are handed over only to the two or three people whose photos are on the child's pick-up card. Furniture is rounded, plug points are covered, and the water is RO-filtered. We are happy to show you all of this on your visit.

faq.q: What does my child need to bring, and what about food?
faq.a: A water bottle and a small tiffin with home food for the 11 o'clock snack — fruit, paratha, idli, poha, anything without chocolates or chips. Daycare children bring lunch or take ours at ₹600 a month (dal, rice, roti, sabzi, curd, with fruit at 4:30). Please tell us about any allergy in the admission form; we keep nut-free days when a child needs them.

faq.q: What documents are needed for admission?
faq.a: The child's birth certificate, the child's Aadhaar if made, Aadhaar of both parents, four passport photos of the child and two each of the parents and of anyone who will pick up the child, and the vaccination card. The form takes ten minutes at the office, or we can send it on WhatsApp to fill at home.

faq.q: My child cries a lot and is not toilet trained — is that a problem?
faq.a: Not at all; most children arrive this way. For the first week a parent or grandparent may sit in the class, and we settle the child over short days before the full timing. Toilet training is done calmly by the didi, with a changing room for diapers in Play Group and Nursery, and no child is ever scolded for an accident.

faq.q: What is the total fee for a year, and how do we pay?
faq.a: For Nursery, for example: ₹3,000 admission (one time) plus ₹2,000 a month for 12 months, plus books and the admission kit. Fees can be paid monthly, quarterly or for the year by UPI, card or cash at the office, and we send a receipt on WhatsApp for every payment. There is a 5% concession for paying the full year in April and for a second sibling.

political.tagline: Your area's voice, from your own gali
political.about: We are a team of karyakartas working in Ward 14 and the nearby villages, led by a man who grew up here and still lives in the same mohalla. Our work is simple: hear the problem face to face, write it down, take it to the right officer and keep following up till the file moves. faq.q: How do I reach you with a problem?

faq.q: Which areas do you work in?

faq.q: Is there any fee or chanda for this help?

faq.q: Can you help with a ration card, pension or Ayushman card?

faq.q: Can you come to our colony or village?

faq.q: Do you deliver, and how do I pay?

reviews.text: My flat was lying vacant for a year. They found a doctor's family as tenants, sent me the police verification and the agreement on WhatsApp, and the rent reaches my account on the 5th every month. They even got the geyser repaired and sent the bill.

faq.q: What is your brokerage and when is it paid?
faq.a: For sale and purchase it is the standard 1 percent of the deal value from each side, told to you in writing before the first visit. For rentals it is one month's rent from the tenant and one from the owner. Nothing is paid until the agreement is signed; a part comes at agreement and the rest at registry or key handover.

faq.q: Do you check the property papers yourselves?
faq.a: Yes. Before we take you for a visit we look at the registry chain, mutation or khatauni, colony approval, electricity and tax dues, and whether any bank loan or court stay is on the property. For the final deal we arrange a written opinion from a property lawyer, which costs around ₹2,500 to ₹5,000 and is worth every rupee.

faq.q: Can you help me get a home loan on the property?
faq.a: Yes. Once you shortlist, we send the property papers to two or three banks together so you get sanction letters to compare. We help with your income documents, sit with the bank valuer at the site and follow up till disbursal. The bank decides the rate and approval, not us, and we never promise one.

faq.q: I live in another city. Can I buy or sell through you without coming?
faq.a: Most of it, yes. We do video visits on WhatsApp, share papers as PDFs and keep you on call during bargaining. For the registry you have to be present or give a registered power of attorney to a relative; we guide you on that too. Several NRI owners rent out and sell through us this way.

faq.q: How long does it take to sell a flat or plot?
faq.a: A fairly priced flat in a settled colony usually finds a buyer in 4 to 10 weeks; plots and shops can take 2 to 4 months. We value it from actual recent deals in your area, not a hopeful number, and tell you honestly if the asking price needs to come down.

faq.q: Can I see properties on a Sunday or in the evening?
faq.a: Yes. Site visits run from 9 am to 7 pm on all days including Sunday; message us a day ahead with the properties you want to see and we plan the route so you cover three or four in one trip. Office walk-in is Monday to Saturday.

faq.q: Do you deliver at home, and what is the charge?
faq.a: Yes, within about 6 km of Station Road. Delivery is free on orders above ₹499 and ₹30 below that. Send your location on WhatsApp and we confirm the time — usually 35 to 45 minutes.

faq.q: Is the kitchen veg and non-veg together?
faq.a: No. Veg and non-veg are cooked in separate sections with separate utensils and tandoor skewers. Jain and no onion-garlic food can be made on request — tell us when you order.

faq.q: Can I book a table for a family dinner?
faq.a: Yes. Message us the date, time and number of people on WhatsApp. For groups of 10 or more, or the private room, please book a day ahead, especially on weekends.

faq.q: How far ahead should I give a party order?
faq.a: For up to 50 people, one day's notice is enough; for larger functions please give us two to three days so we can plan the staff and the tandoor. A 30% advance confirms the order.

faq.q: Do you serve breakfast or only lunch and dinner?
faq.a: We open at 11:00. Lunch thali runs 12:00 to 15:30, snacks and the full à la carte menu all day, and the tandoor is lit from 18:00 to 22:30.

faq.q: How can I pay?
faq.a: Cash, UPI and all debit or credit cards at the counter. For delivery and party orders, UPI on the WhatsApp number works best; a GST bill is available on request.

reviews.name: Sunita M., homemaker
reviews.text: Our tanker water tasted bitter and three plumbers gave three opinions. He came with a TDS meter, showed 1,100 on the screen and suggested the RO with mineraliser. Installed in two days, bill came on WhatsApp, and he still replies when I ask about the filter light.

reviews.name: Rajesh, electrical shop owner
reviews.text: I was buying inverters from a wholesaler with no bill and no support. He set up the company counter in my shop with a display board, explained the scheme sheet properly and now sends the month's offer on WhatsApp on the 1st. Margins are clear and complaints get picked up.

reviews.name: Fr. Thomas, school principal
reviews.text: We needed drinking water for 400 students and a budget we could defend to the committee. He surveyed the site, tested the borewell and gave a 100 LPH quotation with the AMC cost written out. Installation finished in the summer holidays as promised.

faq.q: Can you send a quotation on WhatsApp?
faq.a: Yes. Send the product name and quantity, or just tell me your need (family size, water source, load), and a written company quotation with model number, price, GST and warranty comes back on WhatsApp the same working day.

faq.q: Do I have to pay you or the company?
faq.a: Never to me personally. Payment goes to the company's account by UPI, bank transfer or card against the invoice, and some products have 6-month or 9-month EMI through the company's finance partner.

faq.q: Will I get a proper GST bill and warranty card?
faq.a: Yes. Every order is billed by the company with GST; the invoice is your warranty document, and I register the product under your mobile number so service calls are easy.

faq.q: How long does installation take after I order?
faq.a: Purifiers, geysers and chimneys are usually installed within 48 hours of delivery in town and 3–4 days in nearby villages. Commercial RO plants take 7–10 days after the advance, including site preparation.

faq.q: Is there a better rate for bulk or for a dealer?
faq.a: Yes. From ten units onwards there is a bulk slab, and appointed dealers get the dealer price list with monthly schemes. Tell me the quantity and I confirm the current scheme with the company before quoting.

faq.q: What happens if the product has a problem after six months?
faq.a: Message me the invoice number and the issue. I register the complaint with the company service team, share the ticket number with you and follow it till the technician visits — you do not have to call the toll-free line yourself.

reviews.name: Priya M., bride
reviews.text: The trial made all the difference; the first look was too heavy for my taste and they changed the base and the lip shade without any fuss. On the wedding day the makeup stayed through the pheras at 2 am and my dupatta did not move once.

reviews.name: Rahul, bank employee
reviews.text: I come every three weeks for a haircut and beard trim. They remember how I like the fade, the razor is opened in front of me, and ₹299 is honest for the work. Never had to wait more than ten minutes with a WhatsApp booking.

reviews.name: Sunita D., teacher
reviews.text: I had very frizzy hair after years of straightening at home. They said no to keratin on the first visit because the hair was too damaged, did two hair spas first, and only then the smoothening. It has been three months and it still looks good.

faq.q: Do I need an appointment or can I walk in?
faq.a: Walk-ins are welcome on weekdays, but Saturdays, Sundays and the week before Diwali and Karwa Chauth are fully booked, so send us the service and a time on WhatsApp and we confirm within a few minutes.

faq.q: Which products do you use on hair and skin?
faq.a: Professional salon brands only; the stylist shows you the bottle before starting. If your skin is sensitive or you have had a reaction before, tell us and we do a patch test the day before colour or a facial.

faq.q: Is the salon for women only?
faq.a: We are unisex. There is a separate ladies' section with its own door for waxing, facials and bridal work, and two chairs in the front for men's haircuts, beard shaping and clean-ups.

faq.q: How early should I book for bridal makeup?
faq.a: Four to six weeks before the wedding, so we can fit the trial two to three weeks ahead and any pre-bridal facials or hair spa in between. A ₹3,000 advance holds the date; the balance is paid on the day.

faq.q: Do you give home service?
faq.a: Yes, for bridal and function work: bride and family makeup, hairstyles and saree draping at home or the venue. Regular haircuts and waxing are done at the salon only. Home service is charged extra depending on distance; tell us the venue.

faq.q: What does a service cost and how do I pay?
faq.a: Rates are on the board and on this page; message us for anything not listed and we reply with the price before you come. Pay by cash, UPI or card at the counter; bridal bookings take an advance by UPI.

offer.text: New families who register between Navratri and Diwali pay no ₹200 enrolment fee and receive the printed samaj directory and two sammelan family passes free with their first-year membership.

reviews.name: Mahesh P., father of the groom
reviews.text: We booked the Samaj Bhawan for my son's reception at the member rate and saved nearly ₹10,000 against the marriage garden we had seen. The kitchen block with four LPG points made our halwai's work easy, and the dharamshala rooms upstairs took in all 30 baraatis from Jaipur. Secretary ji himself came at 7 in the morning to open the gate.

reviews.name: Pooja S., B.Sc. nursing student
reviews.text: When my father's shop was closed for months the samiti paid my second-year fees from the chhatravritti fund and I borrowed all my books from the book bank. Nobody made us feel small about asking. I was called on stage at the sammelan this year as a topper, and I now volunteer at the book bank on Sundays.

reviews.name: Rekha J., mahila mandal member
reviews.text: We registered my daughter's bio-data with the rishta cell in March. Only four families were introduced, all of them after asking us first, and the fourth one is now her sasural. What I liked most is that nothing went on Facebook or any matrimony site; everything stayed within the samaj.

faq.q: Who can become a member and what does it cost?
faq.a: Any family of the samaj living in the city or the nearby tehsils can join. Annual family membership is ₹501 for the financial year and covers parents, spouse and unmarried children at one address; life membership is a one-time ₹11,000. Message us on WhatsApp with your name and mohalla and a karyakarta from your area will bring the form to your home.

faq.q: How do we book the Samaj Bhawan for a wedding?
faq.a: Send the date and function type on WhatsApp. If the date is free we hold it for 48 hours; it is confirmed when the ₹5,000 advance reaches the samiti's bank account and a receipt is issued. Members pay ₹21,000 per day and non-member families ₹31,000. Dates around Dev Uthani Ekadashi and the winter wedding season fill 6 to 8 months ahead, so book early.

faq.q: How does the Vivah Parichay rishta cell work?
faq.a: Register the bio-data with two photos at the office or on WhatsApp for ₹251 a year. It stays in a private register with the rishta cell, two senior couples of the samaj. When a profile matches, both families are asked separately before any detail is shared, and nothing is posted on any website or social media. Registered families also get first entry to the winter parichay sammelan.

faq.q: Is there help for students, and how do we apply?
faq.a: Yes. Applications for fee support and hostel contribution are taken from 1 to 31 July with the latest marksheet and the college fee slip; the education committee decides in August and the amount is paid directly to the college. The book bank is open every Saturday and Sunday from 10:00 to 13:00 and lends school, JEE, NEET, CUET and banking exam books for one academic year.

faq.q: What happens if a member family has a death or a medical emergency?
faq.a: Call the emergency number on this page at any hour. The karyakarta for your mohalla reaches the house or hospital, the samiti arranges blood donors from the members' list, and the Bhawan's bartan bhandar and chairs are given free of charge for the tehrvi or shanti path of a member family.

faq.q: Where does the money go and can we see the accounts?
faq.a: Every membership, booking and donation is entered in a numbered receipt book and banked in the samiti's account. The accounts are audited every year by a chartered accountant who is a member, read out at the AGM on the sammelan morning, and the summary is posted in the members' WhatsApp group. Any member can ask to see the ledgers at the office.

hours.time: Any time, call the number on this page

samaj.address: Samaj Bhawan, Plot 4, Civil Lines Road, near Gandhi Chowk
samaj.botPersona: Polite, warm sahayak of the samaj office who talks like a helpful karyakarta: respectful to elders, clear about dates, rates and documents, protective of families' private details, and replies in Hindi or English as the member writes.
samaj.botKnowledge: Can answer about annual and life membership (fees, who is covered, how to join, directory and WhatsApp group), Samaj Bhawan booking (member and non-member rates, capacity, advance, timing, what is included, kitchen and parking), dharamshala rooms (non-AC, AC and dormitory rates, block booking, check-in, ID needed), the Vivah Parichay rishta cell (registration fee, how bio-data is kept private, how introductions are made, the winter parichay sammelan), the annual sammelan (date, family pass rates, programme, registration deadline), bartan bhandar and chair rental (set sizes, deposit, delivery, washing charge), the chhatravritti and book bank (application window, documents, eligibility, book bank timings), mahila mandal and yuva mandal activities, support in illness and bereavement including the emergency number and blood donor list, the office hours and address, how donations are receipted and accounts shared, and the current Navratri to Diwali membership offer. For rishta details, hall dates and donations it collects the family's name, mohalla and phone number and hands over to the office bearer rather than confirming anything itself.

school.jobTitle: Nursery to Class 12, CBSE, English medium
school.tagline: Every child known by name, every day
school.about: We are a co-educational English-medium school from Nursery to Class 12, running on the CBSE syllabus with Hindi as the second language and Sanskrit or Computer Science as the third-language choice. Our campus on the bypass road has airy classrooms, a library, two science labs, a computer lab, a games field and a shaded play area for the little ones, with school buses running on fixed routes across the town and nearby villages. Families choose us for the middle path: serious studies with regular tests and homework, but also sports, music, art and stage time for every child, not just the toppers. Class sizes are kept small enough that the class teacher knows each child's strengths and weak spots, and parents hear from us every month, not only at report-card time.

products.name: Pre-Primary: Nursery, LKG, UKG
products.desc: The first years of school, built around play: rhymes, stories, blocks, colours and outdoor time, with letters and numbers coming in gently through UKG. Half day, with a snack break and a nap corner for Nursery.
features: Two teachers and one didi per section
Separate play area with soft flooring
Phonics-based reading from LKG
Monthly activity sheet sent home

products.name: Primary: Class 1 to 5
products.desc: English, Hindi, Maths, EVS and Computers, taught by subject-trained teachers with a class teacher who stays with the section for the whole year. Reading hour in the library every week and one sports period every day.
features: NCERT books with our own worksheets
Weekly class test, no surprise exams
Handwriting and spoken-English practice
Diary signed by the teacher daily

products.name: Middle School: Class 6 to 8
products.desc: Science, Social Science and Maths get serious here, with lab periods, map work and project weeks. Sanskrit or Computer Science as third language, and house competitions in debate, quiz and sports.
features: Science lab practicals twice a month
Computer lab with one child per system
Two formal exams plus monthly tests
Remedial class after school for weak subjects

products.name: Secondary: Class 9 and 10 (Board)
products.desc: Two years aimed squarely at the Class 10 board exam. Syllabus finishes by December, followed by three full pre-boards with CBSE-pattern answer sheets checked and returned with written remarks.
features: Three pre-board exams, CBSE pattern
Sample papers and previous years' questions
Doubt class every Saturday
Career talk and stream guidance in Class 10

features: PCM or PCB with English and an optional subject
Lab practical record completed in school hours
Weekly objective test on the week's topics
Small sections, so every doubt gets heard

products.name: Senior Secondary: Commerce (Class 11-12)

Maths or IP as the fourth subject
Monthly case-study tests in Business Studies

features: Choose two activities per day
Trained coaches for football and skating
Daily juice and fruit break included
Camp T-shirt and certificate

services.name: Admission counselling
services.desc: A 20-minute sit-down with the coordinator: the right class for your child's age, documents, fees and what the first month looks like.

services.name: Library and reading hour
services.desc: Story books in English and Hindi for the young ones, reference and NCERT exemplar sets for seniors; every class gets a library period each week.

services.name: Sports and games
services.desc: Football, kho-kho, kabaddi, badminton and athletics on our own field, with an annual sports day and inter-house matches every term.

services.name: Music, dance and art
services.desc: Tabla, keyboard, folk and classical dance and drawing classes in the timetable, with the annual function and Independence Day programme as the stage.

services.name: Parent app and monthly PTM
services.desc: Attendance, homework, test marks and circulars on the parent app; a parent-teacher meeting on the first Saturday of every month.

services.name: Medical room and safety
services.desc: A nurse on campus during school hours, first-aid in every bus, CCTV in corridors and at gates, and visitors signed in at the reception.

offer.title: Admissions open: no admission fee for the first 50 forms
offer.text: Register before 31 January for the new session and we waive the ₹5,000 to ₹8,000 admission fee; siblings of current students get 10% off the monthly tuition fee for the whole year.

reviews.name: Priya Sharma, mother of a Class 3 student
reviews.text: My daughter was shy and barely spoke in her last school. Here the class teacher noticed within a month and gave her small roles in the morning assembly. Now she reads the news in English on stage. The diary is signed every single day, so I always know what happened in class.

reviews.name: Rakesh Yadav, father of a Class 10 student
reviews.text: The three pre-boards made the real difference for my son. The answer sheets came back with remarks on where marks were being lost, and the Saturday doubt class was free, no separate coaching needed. We saved on tuition fees outside and he was far more confident in the board exam.

reviews.name: Meena and Sunil Verma, parents of Nursery and Class 6 students
reviews.text: Two children, one bus, and the lady attendant knows both by name. The live bus location on the app means I am not standing at the gate for twenty minutes. Only wish the canteen had more options, but the tiffin break is well managed.

faq.q: What is the age for Nursery admission?
faq.a: The child should be 3 years old by 31 March of the admission year; LKG is 4+ and UKG is 5+ on the same date. We can take a child a few months younger into Nursery after a short interaction with the pre-primary teacher.

faq.q: Which documents do we need to submit?
faq.a: Birth certificate, four passport-size photos of the child and one each of both parents, Aadhaar copies of the child and parents, address proof, and for Class 2 onwards the previous year's report card and the Transfer Certificate from the last school. Caste or EWS certificate only if you are applying under a reserved category.

faq.q: Is there any entrance test?
faq.a: No test up to Class 1; we meet the child and the parents for about 15 minutes. From Class 2 to 9 there is a short written check in English, Hindi and Maths so we place the child correctly and plan remedial help if needed. Class 11 admission is on the Class 10 marks and the stream chosen.

faq.q: Can the fee be paid in instalments?
faq.a: Yes. Tuition fee is collected quarterly (April, July, October, January) at the school office or through the parent app by UPI or card. Paying the full year in April gets a 5% discount on tuition. Bus fee is monthly or quarterly, as you prefer.

faq.q: Does the school bus come to our area?
faq.a: We run nine fixed routes covering the town and the villages along the main highway, up to about 15 km from school. Send us your locality on WhatsApp and we will tell you the nearest stop, the pick-up time and the monthly charge for that route.

faq.q: Which board does the school follow, and what about Hindi?
faq.a: We follow the CBSE syllabus with NCERT books from Class 1 to 12. The medium of instruction is English; Hindi is taught as a compulsory second language till Class 10, and Sanskrit or Computer Science is the third-language option from Class 6 to 8.

security.tagline: Verified guards, supervised shifts, no empty post
security.about: We are a licensed security and housekeeping agency based near the Collectorate, deploying trained guards, gunmen, lady guards and housekeeping staff to housing societies, offices, factories, hospitals, schools, shops and events across the city and nearby industrial areas. Every person we post is police-verified with Aadhaar, photo and address on file, trained for a week on gate control, visitor register, fire safety and basic first aid, and sent in full uniform with ID card and whistle on day one. A field supervisor visits each site on every shift, checks the register and the duty log, and reports to you on WhatsApp the same day. If a guard is on leave, a relief guard reaches before the shift starts; you get one clear monthly invoice with PF and ESIC paid, and a single number to call at 2 a.m. if anything goes wrong.

offer.title: Diwali-season contract offer
offer.text: Sign a 12-month society or office contract before 31 October and the one-time deployment and uniform charge of ₹2,500 per post is waived; the first supervisor report comes within 24 hours of deployment.

reviews.name: Sunita M., society secretary
reviews.text: We shifted to them after our old agency kept leaving the gate empty on Sundays. In seven months there has not been a single morning without a guard, and the supervisor actually comes at night and signs the register. The visitor app with the photo entry settled a lot of committee arguments.

reviews.name: Rakesh J., factory owner
reviews.text: Two 12-hour posts at my unit on the industrial estate. The material gate-pass register is maintained properly and I get a WhatsApp photo of the night log every morning. When one guard left, the replacement was at the gate the same evening.

reviews.name: Dr. Neha P., clinic owner
reviews.text: Took one housekeeping attendant and a day guard for the clinic. The washrooms are cleaned on a checklist that I sign, and the guard manages the token queue and the ambulance entry calmly. Invoice comes on the 1st with PF challan attached.

faq.q: Is every guard police-verified?
faq.a: Yes. Before posting, each guard's Aadhaar, photo, address and police verification form are collected, and a copy of the file is sent to you on WhatsApp. For gunmen we also keep a copy of the arms licence.

faq.q: What happens if the guard does not turn up?
faq.a: The guard has to report absence to the supervisor by 5 a.m. for a morning shift and by 5 p.m. for a night shift. A relief guard from our roster reaches your site before the shift starts. If a post stays empty, that day is deducted from your bill.

faq.q: Can I take just one guard or just one sweeper?
faq.a: Yes. One guard for a shop or house, or one housekeeping attendant for a small office, is fine on a monthly contract. For a single 8-hour post the rate is ₹15,500 per month for a guard and ₹13,500 for housekeeping.

faq.q: What is included in the monthly rate?
faq.a: Salary, PF, ESIC, weekly-off relief, uniform, ID card, whistle and torch, supervisor visits, and the replacement guarantee. GST is extra on the invoice. Items like a visitor app subscription, walkie-talkies or a guard cabin are quoted separately.

faq.q: Is there a minimum contract period or a notice period?
faq.a: Monthly contracts with one month's notice on either side. Event duty is booked per day. For a short requirement of 15 days or more, such as a construction site or an exhibition, ask us for a fixed-period quote.

faq.q: How soon can you deploy?
faq.a: Unarmed guards and housekeeping staff within 3 working days of the site visit; lady guards within 5 days; licensed gunmen within 7 days. For events, book at least 3 days before with 50% advance.

reviews.name: Priya M., IT professional
reviews.text: I booked the deep tissue for my laptop shoulders and the therapist actually asked where it hurt before starting instead of doing a set routine. Lady therapist, separate wing, fresh sheets on the bed — I could see them being changed. Went back the next week.

reviews.name: Rajesh K., cloth merchant
reviews.text: After the Surat trip my legs were dead. Foot reflexology and a steam, forty-five minutes, no one rushed me and the tulsi tea at the end was a nice touch. Parking in the plaza basement is easy, which matters on MG Road.

reviews.name: Neha & Arjun, anniversary
reviews.text: Took the couple ritual for our fifth anniversary. Candles, soft music, both beds in one room, and they had the cake we asked for waiting with the tea. Only wish the steam room were a little bigger.

faq.q: Do I need to book in advance?
faq.a: Yes, please — we have six rooms and one couple room, and evenings and weekends fill up. Message us the treatment and a time on WhatsApp; we confirm within a few minutes. Weekday afternoons often have walk-in slots for head or foot massage.

faq.q: Can I ask for a lady or a gents therapist?
faq.a: Yes. Female guests are attended by lady therapists in the ladies' wing by default; male guests get a male therapist. Tell us any preference when booking and we arrange it.

faq.q: What should I wear or bring?
faq.a: Nothing special. We give disposable wear, slippers, a towel set and a locker for your things. Come 10 minutes early, avoid a heavy meal just before, and skip jewellery if you can.

faq.q: What if the pressure is too much or too little?
faq.a: Just say so — the therapist checks once at the start and once mid-way, and will change it any time you ask. Nobody has to 'bear it'.

faq.q: Is massage okay during pregnancy or after surgery?
faq.a: Please ask your doctor first and tell us before the session. We do not do deep tissue or abhyanga in pregnancy or within six weeks of surgery; a gentle head or foot massage may be possible with your doctor's okay.

faq.q: How do I pay, and can I reschedule?
faq.a: Cash, UPI and cards at the counter; packages and couple bookings are paid in advance. You can reschedule free up to 3 hours before your slot; a no-show on a couple booking forfeits the advance.

spa.address: 2nd Floor, Galaxy Plaza, above the pharmacy, MG Road — basement parking
spa.botPersona: A soft-spoken spa front-desk host — polite, unhurried, helps you pick a treatment and a slot, and never gives medical advice.
spa.botKnowledge: The full treatment list with price, duration, pressure and what each is best for (Swedish, deep tissue, abhyanga, head-neck-shoulder, foot reflexology, body scrub, couple ritual, monthly package); add-ons like steam, hair wash and combining a scrub with a massage; lady or gents therapist choice and the ladies' wing; what to wear and bring, lockers and disposable wear; the Diwali gift voucher offer and how vouchers are sent and redeemed; hours, last-booking time, the couple room availability and how to book on WhatsApp; address, landmark and basement parking; reschedule and no-show rules; payment by cash, UPI and card with packages paid in advance; office chair-massage and hotel visits by prior booking. For pregnancy, surgery or any health condition the bot asks the guest to consult their doctor and to inform the therapist — it never promises relief or a result.

student.tagline: Learning daily, and helping you learn too
student.about: I am a second-year B.Tech Computer Science student at the government engineering college in our city, originally from a small town where I did my schooling in a Hindi-medium school. Alongside my own classes I teach Maths and Science to Class 6–10 students in the evenings, share my handwritten notes as PDFs, and take small design and coding gigs — posters, PPTs, Python mini projects. Parents like that I explain the way a senior would, in simple Hinglish, with the exact examples that come in board papers. Right now I am also looking for a summer internship in web or app development and am always up for a hackathon, quiz or college fest team.

offer.title: Board exam season: free trial week
offer.text: Try Class 9–10 tuition for one week free before you decide, and get any notes PDF at ₹99 till the board exams finish.

reviews.name: Mrs. Sunita Verma, parent of a Class 10 student
reviews.text: My son used to be scared of Trigonometry. In two months he started solving the NCERT exercise on his own. The weekly test sheet with corrections comes home every Saturday, so I always know where he stands.

reviews.name: Aman, B.Tech classmate
reviews.text: Took help for our DBMS mini project. The code was clean, the report was in the exact college format, and the viva practice call the night before really saved me. Explained every line patiently.

reviews.name: Priya, college fest coordinator
reviews.text: Got all our fest posters and the sponsor PPT designed in two days. Both Hindi and English versions, print sizes correct the first time. Very quick replies on WhatsApp even during exams.

faq.q: Which college and year are you in?
faq.a: I am in the second year of B.Tech Computer Science at the government engineering college in our city. I did Class 12 (PCM) from a state board school, so I know both the CBSE and state board patterns well.

faq.q: Do you come home for tuition, or is it online?
faq.a: Both. Home visits are possible within about 5 km of my hostel, usually between 5 pm and 9 pm. For other areas or during my exam weeks, we shift to online classes on Google Meet with a digital whiteboard.

faq.q: How are the notes delivered after payment?
faq.a: Pay by UPI, send the screenshot on WhatsApp, and the PDF reaches you within an hour, usually faster. If any page is unclear or missing, I send a corrected file free.

faq.q: Can you make my whole project so I just submit it?
faq.a: I build the project with you, not for you. You get working code, a report and a viva practice session so that you can explain every part yourself. This keeps you safe in the viva and you actually learn something.

faq.q: Are you available for internships or part-time work?
faq.a: Yes, as long as it fits around college. I am looking for a summer internship in web or app development and can take remote part-time design or data entry work right now. Share the details on WhatsApp.

faq.q: Can we study together for university exams?
faq.a: Of course. For my own semester subjects — Data Structures, DBMS, Maths III — I run weekend group study sessions in the library. Message me the subject and date, and I will add you to the group.

student.botPersona: Polite, friendly student voice — like a sincere senior helping juniors; simple Hinglish, honest about what I can and cannot do, never promises marks or grades.
student.botKnowledge: Can answer who I am (college, year, subjects, hometown), tuition details for Class 6–10 (fees per month, batch size, home or online, timings, free trial week), which notes PDFs are available with prices and how they are delivered after UPI payment, design and PPT gig rates and turnaround, Python/C mini project process and timeline, science model help, group study timings for university subjects, and that I am open to internships, part-time work, volunteering and fest or quiz teams. For anything about exact availability on a date, home-visit distance, or custom project quotes, the bot asks the person to share details and says I will reply personally on WhatsApp.

sweets.tagline: Desi ghee mithai, made fresh every morning
sweets.about: We are a family-run sweet shop and bakery on Main Market Road, feeding this town's festivals, weddings and evening chai for two generations. Our halwais start at 5 am so the kaju katli, motichoor laddoo and rasmalai on the counter were made that same morning — in pure desi ghee, with khoya we thicken ourselves and no colours or essences we would not serve our own children. From a 250 g box for a guest to 500 laddoo boxes for a wedding, every order gets the same khoya, the same ghee and the same care in packing. Walk in and taste before you buy, or send your list on WhatsApp and we deliver across the city.

offer.title: Diwali early-bird: 10% off gift boxes
offer.text: Book 20 or more Diwali gift boxes 7 days before the festival and get 10% off plus free logo stickers for your company.

reviews.name: Priyanka M., bride's mother
reviews.text: We ordered 300 shagun boxes of motichoor laddoo and kaju katli for my daughter's wedding. Every box was packed identically, delivered to the venue a day early as promised, and the laddoos were still soft on the third day. Relatives from Delhi asked where we got them.

reviews.name: Sandeep K., HR manager
reviews.text: Our office takes 120 Diwali boxes from them every year. They printed our logo on the sticker, kept to the budget we gave and sent a sample box first so we could check. The dry sweets travelled fine to our Pune team.

reviews.name: Rekha, regular customer
reviews.text: I buy their rasmalai every Sunday — the rabri is thick and not overly sweet. The besan laddoo tastes like my nani's, which I do not say about any shop. Only wish they opened earlier on Sunday.

faq.q: Do you take orders for weddings and large functions?
faq.a: Yes. Send us the items, quantity, packing style (per box or loose) and the delivery date on WhatsApp. We confirm the price and send a sample if you want. Orders above 25 kg need 3 days' notice and a 30% advance.

faq.q: How long do the sweets stay fresh?
faq.a: Milk sweets like rasmalai and rasgulla are best within 2 days refrigerated; khoya sweets like barfi and gulab jamun 4 to 5 days; dry sweets like kaju katli, anjeer roll and besan laddoo 7 to 10 days; namkeen 3 weeks in a sealed pouch. We write the best-before date on every box.

faq.q: Do you deliver at home?
faq.a: Yes, across the city for WhatsApp orders placed before 5 pm. Delivery is free above ₹999 within 5 km; otherwise ₹40 to ₹80 depending on distance. For outstation courier we send only dry sweets and namkeen.

faq.q: Can I get gift packing with my company's name?
faq.a: Yes. Rigid boxes, hampers and trays are packed here, and we can print a sticker or tag with your logo for orders of 20 boxes or more. Share the logo and we send a photo of the sample box for approval.

faq.q: Do you make sugar-free or vegan sweets?
faq.a: Sugar-free anjeer roll, dry-fruit laddoo and kaju katli (with a sugar substitute) are made on request with one day's notice; please check with your doctor if you are diabetic. Besan laddoo and dry-fruit laddoo can be made without milk solids for vegan guests.

faq.q: Can I order by weight or only in boxes?
faq.a: Both. At the counter everything is sold by weight from 100 g, packed in our standard box. For gifting we have 250 g, 500 g and 1 kg rigid boxes. Payment by cash, UPI or card at the shop; UPI for WhatsApp orders.

It takes the item list, quantity, date and address and hands the order to the owner on WhatsApp; it never promises a discount or a delivery slot the owner has not confirmed.

tailor.about: We are a family-run ladies and gents tailoring boutique in Main Market, stitching suits, blouses, lehengas, shirts, trousers and kurta-pyjama for the families of this city since the shop was a single sewing machine. Bring your own fabric or choose from the lining, lace and dress material on our shelves; measurements are taken in a separate ladies' cabin, and for bridal orders we come to your home. Every stitched garment gets a trial before the final finish and is handed over pressed, on the date written on your slip. Alterations on ready-made clothes are welcome, however small the job.

reviews.name: Neha S., bride
reviews.text: My lehenga had 24 panels of heavy work and the first trial on the plain shell showed the waist needed to come in by an inch; they fixed it and the second trial fitted perfectly. The can-can gave the flare I wanted without the weight, and I could sit through the whole reception.

reviews.name: Rajesh, bank officer
reviews.text: I gave them fabric for four shirts and two trousers before a transfer. Collars are properly fused, the sleeve length was tried on me before finishing, and everything was ready on the Saturday written on the slip. Better fit than any ready-made I have bought.

reviews.name: Meena K., teacher
reviews.text: The blouse was stitched from a photo I sent on WhatsApp, with the boat neck and the back dori exactly like the picture. The padding is neat and does not show. Two kurtis I got altered the same day for a function that evening.

faq.q: How many days does stitching take?
faq.a: A blouse takes 4 to 6 days, a suit 7 to 10, a gown 10 to 12 and a bridal lehenga 20 to 25. In the wedding months and before Diwali the queue is longer, so the exact date is written on your slip when you place the order.

faq.q: Can you stitch a design from a photo?
faq.a: Yes. Send the photo on WhatsApp and we reply with the fabric length needed, what embroidery or lining it will take and the price, before you buy anything.

faq.q: How much fabric should I bring?
faq.a: Roughly 0.8 m for a blouse, 2.5 m kameez plus 2.5 m salwar for a suit, 1.6 m for a shirt, 1.2 m for a trouser and 6 to 7 m for a full-flare lehenga. Message us the design and your height and we confirm the metres.

faq.q: Is there a trial before delivery?
faq.a: Every stitched garment gets a trial before the final seam, usually two or three days before delivery. Lehengas and gowns get two trials. Small changes at the trial are free.

faq.q: Do you alter ready-made clothes bought elsewhere?
faq.a: Yes, jeans, trousers, kurtis, shirts, blazers and sarees. Bring the garment and the shoes or belt you will wear with it; length and hooks are done the same day if you come before 5 pm.

faq.q: How do I pay and is there an advance?
faq.a: Half the stitching charge as advance at the order, the rest at delivery, by cash or UPI. Fabric bought from the shop is paid for at the time of purchase.

teacher.jobTitle: Maths & Science Teacher | Home, Online & Small-Group Tuition, Class 6 – 12
teacher.about: We teach Maths and Science to students of Class 6 to 12 (CBSE and State Board) at the student's home, online on video call, and in small batches of six at our study room in Teachers Colony, along with a Spoken English course for college students and working adults. Every new student begins with a free trial class and a short diagnostic test, so we start from the chapter where the gaps actually are, not from where the school syllabus happens to be. Classes run on a fixed weekly timetable with a short test every Saturday, and parents get a WhatsApp report the same evening with the marks, the weak topics and what we will do about them. We are a postgraduate in Mathematics with a B.Ed. and twelve years of school and private teaching, and we take only as many students as we can personally attend to.

products.name: Home Tuition — Maths, Class 9 & 10
products.desc: One-to-one Maths at your home, three days a week, following the school's chapter order with NCERT, RD Sharma and previous-year board questions.
features: 3 classes a week, 60 minutes each, fixed days and time
Every chapter closed with a 20-mark test and a corrected answer sheet
Previous 5 years' board questions solved chapter-wise
Saturday test report to parents on WhatsApp

products.name: Home Tuition — Science, Class 9 & 10
products.desc: Physics, Chemistry and Biology taught together at home, with diagrams drawn step by step and numericals practised until the student can do them alone.
features: 3 classes a week; Physics numericals get a dedicated day
Labelled diagrams practised for every Biology chapter
Chemistry equations and reasoning questions drilled before each school test
Practical file and project help included

products.name: Class 11 & 12 Maths — One-to-One
products.desc: Calculus, vectors, probability and matrices taught from the basics, for board exams and as a foundation for JEE Main, CUET and commerce entrance tests.
features: 4 classes a week, 75 minutes, home or online
NCERT fully solved, then board and JEE Main-level practice sets
Fortnightly full-syllabus-till-date test with marked answer sheet
Revision plan for the last 60 days before boards

Homework photographed and checked on WhatsApp

products.desc: Both subjects in one evening batch of maximum six students at our study room, so every child is asked a question in every class and nobody hides at the back.
features: 5 days a week, 90 minutes (Maths 45 + Science 45)
Maximum 6 students, grouped by class
Weekly test every Saturday with ranks shared only with parents
Homework finished in class on two days a week

products.desc: For college students, housewives and working adults who understand English but hesitate to speak it. Small group of eight, every class is 70% speaking, 30% grammar.

Interview, phone-call and presentation practice in the last month

offer.title: Diwali Enrolment Offer
offer.text: Join any home, online or batch course between 1 and 31 October and the first four classes are free; a second child from the same family gets 20% off the monthly fee for the whole session.

reviews.name: Meena K., mother of a Class 10 student
reviews.text: My daughter used to leave the Physics numericals blank in every school test. Sir gave the numericals their own day each week and made her write the formula and units before touching the calculator. The Saturday report on WhatsApp is the best part — I know every week which chapter is weak instead of finding out at the PTM.

reviews.name: Aryan S., Class 12 Commerce
reviews.text: I joined for Class 12 Maths online in July because there was no good teacher in my town. The whiteboard PDFs and the recordings saved me — I revised integration from the recordings three times before pre-boards. He also replies to doubt photos on WhatsApp even at 8 pm, which no school teacher ever did.

reviews.name: Priya R., bank employee
reviews.text: Joined the Spoken English morning batch for ladies because I would freeze when customers spoke in English at the branch. The daily two-minute voice notes felt silly at first but after six weeks I was speaking without translating in my head. Would have liked a few more mock-interview sessions, but the course is honest value for the fee.

faq.q: Which subjects and classes do you teach?
faq.a: Maths and Science for Class 6 to 10 (CBSE and State Board), Maths for Class 11 and 12 (Science and Commerce), and a Spoken English course for college students and adults. We do not teach Social Science, Hindi or languages other than English, but can suggest a trusted colleague for those.

faq.q: Do you come home, or do we come to you, or is it online?
faq.a: All three. Home tuition is available within about 5 km of Teachers Colony (Sector 5 to Sector 12 and the Station Road side). Small-group batches run at our study room in Teachers Colony. Online classes are open to any city; share your area and preferred timing on WhatsApp and we will tell you what is possible.

faq.q: Is there a trial class, and is it free?
faq.a: Yes. The first class plus a 30-minute diagnostic test is free, at home, online or at the study room. Only after that do we suggest a plan and fee, and you decide. There is no registration charge.

faq.q: What is the fee and how is it paid?
faq.a: Home tuition for Class 9 and 10 is ₹3,500 a month per subject, Class 11 and 12 Maths is ₹5,000 a month, online one-to-one is ₹2,800 a month and the Class 6 to 8 batch is ₹1,800 a month for both subjects. Fees are paid monthly by UPI or cash by the 5th, and a receipt is sent on WhatsApp. Taking two subjects or two siblings earns a discount; ask us.

faq.q: My child is weak and has lost confidence. Can you still help?
faq.a: This is actually most of our students. The diagnostic test tells us the real starting point, which is often two or three chapters, or even one class, behind. We go back to that point, build up with extra practice sheets and small wins, and keep the school syllabus moving in parallel. Progress is steady rather than instant, and we tell parents honestly each Saturday where things stand.

faq.q: What if we miss a class?
faq.a: If you inform us at least 3 hours before, the class is adjusted within the same week, usually on Sunday morning. Online students also get the recording. If the teacher has to cancel, the class is always made up and never charged. More than two uninformed absences in a month are not adjusted, so that the timetable stays fair for every student.

temple.tagline: Darshan, seva and prasad — every day, for everyone
temple.about: We are the trust that looks after the old Shiv-Hanuman mandir on Mandir Marg, a temple the town has walked to since our grandparents' time, now run by a registered dharmarth trust of eleven local families. Devotees come for the 5:30 am mangala aarti, Monday rudrabhishek, Tuesday Hanuman chalisa path and the big utsavs of Shivratri, Hanuman Jayanti and Navratri, while families from outside the city book poojas in their name and receive prasad by courier. The temple runs an annakshetra that serves a simple bhojan prasad every afternoon, a 14-room dharamshala for pilgrims and a free Sunday Gita class for children. Every rupee that comes in is receipted, the accounts are read out at the annual sabha and pinned on the notice board, and the pandits who do your seva are the same four Acharyas who have served here for years.

services.desc: Simple bhojan prasad served every afternoon, with sponsored bhandaras on festivals, tithis and family occasions.

services.desc: Shivratri night jagran, Hanuman Jayanti sundarkand, nine days of Navratri garba and Kartik deepotsav, open to the whole town.

services.desc: Nineteen clean rooms and a family hall inside the compound, with hot water, bhojan and a lift to the shikhara road.

services.desc: Give by UPI, bank transfer or at the counter for annadaan, the temple gaushala or the new mandap roof; receipt on the spot.

services.desc: Free Gita shloka and sanskar class for children aged 6 to 14 every Sunday morning, and a bhajan sandhya on the first Saturday of the month.

offer.title: Shravan special: four Monday rudrabhisheks for the price of three
offer.text: Book all four Shravan Mondays together for ₹3,300 instead of ₹4,400; prasad is couriered home after every Monday and your name is read in each sankalp.

reviews.name: Sunita D., devotee in Pune
reviews.text: My mother wanted a Satyanarayan Katha done at her childhood temple and I could not travel. The office booked it on WhatsApp, Acharya ji did the sankalp with her name on a video call, and the prasad box with chunri reached Pune in three days. She cried when she opened it.

reviews.name: Rakesh, sweet shop owner
reviews.text: We sponsored the bhandara on my father's first shraddh. Around 300 people were served puri-sabzi and halwa, the kitchen was spotless and they let my sons serve with their own hands. The receipt and photos came the same evening without my asking.

reviews.name: Meena & Arvind, parents
reviews.text: Did our daughter's mundan here on a Tuesday morning. Pandit ji explained what each mantra meant, the barber was already waiting, and they gave us the side courtyard for forty relatives with chairs and water. Only thing, parking was tight because of the market day.

faq.q: What are the darshan and aarti timings?
faq.a: The temple opens at 5:00 am for mangala aarti at 5:30, closes 12:00 to 4:00 pm after bhog aarti, and opens again till shayan aarti at 9:00 pm. On Shivratri, Hanuman Jayanti and Navratri the doors stay open through the day; festival timings are posted here and on the WhatsApp broadcast a week before.

faq.q: I live in another city. Can I book a pooja in my name?
faq.a: Yes. Send the pooja, the preferred date, the devotee's full name, gotra and the wish for the sankalp on WhatsApp, pay by UPI, and you get the receipt at once. On the day you can join the sankalp on a video call, and the prasad box is couriered the same evening for ₹351, or free with Nitya Seva.

faq.q: How do I donate, and will I get a receipt?
faq.a: At the donation counter, by UPI to the trust's number or by bank transfer to the trust account; the details are sent on request, never asked for in a cold message. A numbered receipt is issued for every donation, and the trust is registered under 80G, so a certificate is given for income-tax purposes on request.

faq.q: Can we sponsor a bhandara for a family occasion?
faq.a: Yes. Message the date and the rough number of people; ₹5,100 covers bhojan prasad for 100 devotees in the annakshetra, cooked in the temple kitchen. Festival-day bhandaras of 500 or more plates need two weeks' notice. Your family is welcome to come and serve.

faq.q: Is there a place to stay near the temple?
faq.a: The trust runs a dharamshala inside the compound with 14 non-AC rooms at ₹600, 4 AC rooms at ₹1,000 and a family hall at ₹1,800 per night. Bring a photo ID for every adult. Rooms fill a month ahead for Shravan and Navratri, so message your dates early.

faq.q: Is there a dress code or anything we should know before visiting?
faq.a: Simple, modest clothes; dhoti-kurta or saree is welcome but not required. Footwear and leather belts are left at the free shoe stand by the gate. Phones on silent inside the garbhagriha, and photography only in the courtyard and mandap. Wheelchair access is through the side ramp near the dharamshala gate.

temple.address: Shri Mandir, Mandir Marg, near Old Bus Stand, Purani Basti
temple.botPersona: Calm, respectful temple office assistant who greets with Namaste, answers in simple Hindi or English, and never promises any result from a pooja.
temple.botKnowledge: Daily darshan and five aarti timings and how they change on festival days; the list of sevas and poojas with prices, duration, what is included and how to book one with name, gotra and date; how outstation devotees join by video call and receive prasad by courier; bhandara and annadaan sponsorship rates and notice needed; dharamshala room types, rates, ID rules and check-in times; how to donate by UPI, bank or counter and that a numbered receipt and 80G certificate are given; festival calendar, Sunday Gita class and bhajan sandhya; address, parking, shoe stand and wheelchair access. The bot does not give astrological advice, does not suggest which pooja will fix a problem, and never shares bank details unprompted; for those it asks the devotee to call the trust office.

offer.title: Wedding Season Trousseau Offer
offer.text: Shop for ₹15,000 or more in sarees, suits or lehengas between 1 November and 31 January and get blouse stitching free on all the pieces, plus a Banarasi dupatta of your choice at half price. Mention the offer on WhatsApp or at the counter.

reviews.name: Sunita M., mother of the bride
reviews.text: We bought the bridal lehenga, eleven gift sarees for the rituals and matching for both sisters from here in two visits. The owner told us clearly which sarees were pure silk and which were art silk, and the prices were written on the tag, no bargaining drama. The blouses were ready four days before the wedding as promised.

reviews.name: Farhan, boutique owner in a nearby town
reviews.text: I take a 50-piece mixed lot of printed sarees and Chanderi suits every month. The lot video comes on WhatsApp before I pay, the GST bill is proper and the parcel reaches by the second day. In one year only two pieces had a weaving fault and both were replaced in the next lot without any argument.

reviews.name: Priya K., school teacher
reviews.text: The handloom cotton sarees are my daily wear now, soft from the first day and the colour has not run even after many washes. Fall-pico was done while I waited. Only wish they had more plain pastel shades in cotton; the staff said they are coming in the next lot.

faq.q: How do I know if a saree is pure silk or art silk?
faq.a: We tell you the exact fabric of every piece before billing and the price tag says it too. Pure silk Banarasi and Kanjivaram pieces carry the Silk Mark tag; soft silk and art silk are labelled as such and priced much lower. If you want, we do the burn test on a loose thread in front of you.

faq.q: Do you sell wholesale, and what is the minimum?
faq.a: Yes. Shops and boutiques can buy assorted lots starting at 20 pieces for synthetic sarees and 10 pieces for suits or silk. Send your shop name and what you sell on WhatsApp; we send catalogue videos and the trade rate sheet, and dispatch by transport or courier with a GST bill after 50% advance.

faq.q: Can I buy a single saree on WhatsApp without visiting?
faq.a: Yes. Tell us the occasion, budget and colour, and we send photos and a short video of 8 to 10 options with prices. Once you choose, pay by UPI and we courier it with fall-pico done. Courier is free within the state on orders above ₹2,000; otherwise ₹80 to ₹150 depending on the location.

faq.q: Do you do fall-pico and blouse stitching?
faq.a: Fall and pico are done in-house, free on sarees above ₹1,000 and ₹60 otherwise, usually while you wait or within a day. Blouse stitching is through our tailor: plain blouse ₹350, designer or padded ₹600 to ₹900, in 5 to 7 days; 10 days in wedding season. Give measurements or an old blouse to copy.

faq.q: What if the colour looks different from the photo, can I exchange?
faq.a: Unused pieces with tags and the original fold can be exchanged within 7 days of delivery for another piece or a credit note; send a photo on WhatsApp first. Pieces with fall-pico or stitching done, and lots sold on wholesale rates, are not exchanged, which is why we send a video in daylight before dispatch.

faq.q: How should I store and wash silk sarees?
faq.a: Dry clean only for Banarasi, Kanjivaram and zari work. Store folded in a muslin or cotton cloth, not plastic, and refold along different lines every few months so the zari does not crack. Cotton sarees can be machine washed cold with mild detergent; wash dark colours separately the first two times.

For custom bridal colours, bulk wedding gift sarees and final wholesale rates, it collects the requirement and hands over to the owner on WhatsApp.

tiffin.tagline: Ghar ka khana, delivered hot every day
tiffin.about: We are a family-run tiffin service cooking from our own kitchen in Shanti Nagar for students, working people, bachelors and families who want proper ghar ka khana without the daily hassle. Every tiffin is cooked the same morning in filtered water and refined-free oil — phulka rotis rolled by hand, dal tempered just before packing, a sabzi that changes every single day so you never eat the same thing twice in a week. We pack in steel or food-grade containers, deliver on our own bikes within 5 km at the same time every day, and let you pause a day on WhatsApp whenever you travel or have a party. Try one meal first; most people who try stay for the month.

offer.text: New customers get their first 6 lunch tiffins (Mon – Sat) for ₹549 instead of ₹660 — if you continue to the monthly plan, the ₹549 is adjusted in it.

reviews.name: Ankit S., software engineer
reviews.text: I have been on their monthly lunch plan for eight months. The sabzi really does change every day — I keep their weekly menu screenshot on my phone. When I went home for Diwali I paused for 9 days on WhatsApp and the days were added to the next month without any argument.

reviews.name: Mrs. Verma, mother of a hostel student
reviews.text: My son is in the engineering hostel and would not eat the mess food. We took the student mini tiffin for him and it comes to the hostel gate at 7:30 pm sharp. The rotis are soft even an hour later and they sent dalia when he had fever and I asked. Worth every rupee for a mother's peace of mind.

reviews.name: Dr. Nisha K., clinic owner
reviews.text: We take 12 office lunch boxes daily for our clinic staff. Boxes arrive sealed by 12:45 with the Jain ones clearly marked, and the Friday kheer has become a small office ritual. I would only ask for a little more variety in the rice days.

faq.q: Which areas do you deliver to, and at what time?
faq.a: We deliver on our own bikes within about 5 km of Shanti Nagar — covering the college road, the station side, the industrial area and the new sector flats. Lunch arrives between 11:30 and 13:30 and dinner between 19:00 and 21:00, at roughly the same time at your address every day. Send your location on WhatsApp and we confirm within an hour.

faq.q: What exactly comes in a tiffin, and does it change?
faq.a: The standard lunch has 4 phulkas, one sabzi, one dal, steamed rice, salad and pickle. Dinner is 3 phulkas, a dry sabzi, dal or kadhi and jeera rice on alternate days. The sabzi and dal run on a weekly cycle — for example rajma on Tuesday, kadhi-pakoda on Thursday, paneer on Saturday — and we share the week's menu every Sunday evening on WhatsApp.

faq.q: Can I pause when I travel or skip a day?
faq.a: Yes. Message 'pause' with the date by 8 pm the night before and that meal is not cooked or charged. Monthly plans allow up to 8 pause days a month and the unused meals carry to your next month. A same-morning cancellation after 9:30 cannot be adjusted because the food is already cooked.

faq.q: Can I try before subscribing, and is there an advance?
faq.a: Order a single lunch or dinner at the daily rate (₹110 / ₹100) with no advance — pay by UPI when the tiffin arrives. New customers can also take the trial week of 6 lunches for ₹549. Monthly plans are paid in advance and the trial amount is adjusted if you continue.

faq.q: Do you make low-oil, Jain or doctor-advised meals?
faq.a: Yes. Our Diet and Recovery meal (₹120) is cooked with minimal oil and no red chilli, and we prepare Jain or no-onion-no-garlic food on request. Write your restrictions once on WhatsApp — things to avoid, salt level, rice or roti preference — and every tiffin follows them. We cook as per your instructions, not as a medical service, so please follow your doctor's advice on what to eat.

faq.q: What about the tiffin box — do I return it? How do I pay?
faq.a: Daily and monthly customers get a 3-tier steel tiffin; our rider collects yesterday's washed box when dropping today's, so please keep it ready. Office and Sunday orders come in sealed disposable boxes with nothing to return. Payment is by UPI — daily customers pay on delivery, monthly plans in advance, offices by weekly or monthly invoice.

tiffin.botKnowledge: The bot can answer what comes in each tiffin (lunch, dinner, mini, non-veg, diet, office box, Sunday thali) with quantity and price, today's and this week's sabzi-dal menu, daily versus monthly rates (₹110 lunch, ₹100 dinner, ₹2,599 monthly lunch, ₹2,399 monthly dinner, ₹4,799 lunch + dinner, ₹1,999 student mini), the trial week offer of 6 lunches for ₹549, delivery area within about 5 km of Shanti Nagar and the lunch and dinner delivery windows, order cut-off times (9:30 am for lunch, 4 pm for dinner, previous evening 8 pm for non-veg, diet and Sunday thali), the pause rule (by 8 pm the night before, up to 8 days a month, carried forward), Jain and low-oil customisation and how to send restrictions, steel-tiffin return and exchange by the rider, office minimums (10 boxes) and invoicing, hostel-gate group delivery (5 tiffins minimum), payment by UPI, address and landmarks. It collects the customer's name, area, meal type, veg or non-veg, start date and any food restrictions and passes them to the owner on WhatsApp; it never promises a delivery time, discount or menu item that the owner has not confirmed, and never gives medical advice about what someone should eat.

transport.tagline: Your goods, loaded right and delivered on time
transport.about: We are a transport and packers-and-movers company working out of Transport Nagar, with our own tempos, 14 ft and 17 ft trucks and 32 ft containers, and tie-up vehicles for everything bigger. Families call us for house shifting within the city and to Delhi, Jaipur, Ahmedabad, Indore and Mumbai; shopkeepers, wholesalers and small factories use us for regular loads, part loads and monthly contract hauling. Every booking gets a written quote on WhatsApp before the vehicle moves, our own trained labour does the packing and loading, and you get the driver's number and location updates till the last carton is unloaded. No broker in between, no surprise charges at the door.

offer.title: Diwali shifting offer
offer.text: Book any 2 BHK or bigger house shifting 7 days in advance before 15 November and packing material (worth about ₹1,500) is free.

reviews.name: Priyanka M., shifted 2 BHK
reviews.text: Four boys came at 8 in the morning and by 2 pm we were in the new flat with the beds already assembled. Not a single glass broke, and the crockery was wrapped piece by piece. The quote on WhatsApp was the final bill.

reviews.name: Mukesh, garment wholesaler
reviews.text: I send 15 – 20 bundles to Delhi every week on their part-load truck. LR comes on WhatsApp the same evening and the goods reach Gandhi Nagar market in two days. Rate has stayed the same for a year.

reviews.name: Rohit S., moved to Pune
reviews.text: Intercity move with a bike. They crated the bike properly, took photos of everything at pickup and the driver called me himself before reaching. One wardrobe handle had come loose, which they fixed on the spot.

faq.q: How is the rate decided?
faq.a: By distance, the vehicle size you need, the volume of goods and whether packing and labour are included. Send photos or a short video of the goods and both addresses on WhatsApp and you get a written quote within an hour; that quote is the final bill unless the goods turn out to be more than shown.

faq.q: Do I have to pack myself?
faq.a: No. For house and office shifting our crew brings the material and packs everything. If you want to pack yourself, book transport-only and we charge for the vehicle and loading labour alone.

faq.q: What if something breaks?
faq.a: Breakage on our packed moves is rare because of the way we wrap and load, but if it happens we settle it at the time of delivery. For intercity moves we recommend transit insurance at 3% of declared value, which covers accident, fire and theft during transit.

faq.q: Can I track where my goods are?
faq.a: Yes. At dispatch you get the driver's number and the vehicle number, the driver shares his live location at each halt, and the office sends a photo at unloading. For commercial loads we also send the LR and e-way bill copy.

faq.q: Do you take small loads to other cities?
faq.a: Yes, part load on our scheduled trucks to Delhi, Jaipur, Ahmedabad, Indore and Mumbai, three departures a week on each route, with a minimum billing of 50 kg. For other cities we check with partner transporters and tell you the rate and transit time.

faq.q: How and when do I pay?
faq.a: 20% advance on UPI or bank transfer confirms the booking and the vehicle. The balance is paid after unloading, by UPI, bank transfer or cash. GST invoice is given for every booking.

reviews.name: Sunita & family, Char Dham Yatra
reviews.text: We were five people including my 68-year-old mother-in-law. The yatra manager arranged a palki at Kedarnath without us asking, hotels at Guptkashi and Badrinath had hot water, and every evening they told us the next day's plan. Not one day felt rushed.

reviews.name: Rohit & Neha, Kerala honeymoon
reviews.text: The same driver stayed with us for all six days and knew every viewpoint in Munnar. The houseboat night was the best part — the cook made fresh karimeen for dinner. Room was decorated with flowers when we reached Kochi, exactly as promised.

reviews.name: Mrs. Verma, school principal
reviews.text: Took 120 students of class 9 and 10 to Jaipur and Agra. The escort handled headcounts at every stop, water and veg meals were on the bus, and the parents got a WhatsApp update each evening. Billing was one clean invoice for the school.

faq.q: What exactly is included in the package price?
faq.a: Every package page lists it, and we send the same inclusions list on WhatsApp before you pay: hotel category, which meals, the vehicle, sightseeing entries and transfers. Flights and trains are extra unless the package says otherwise, and we quote them at the live fare on the day you confirm. GST of 5% is added to the package price.

faq.q: Can you make a custom package for my dates and budget?
faq.a: Yes — tell us the places, dates, number of people and a rough budget per person, and within a day you get a day-by-day plan with hotel options at two or three price levels. Most of our bookings are custom plans built this way, not fixed group departures.

faq.q: What happens if I need to cancel?
faq.a: Cancellation follows the rules of the airline, railway, hotel or operator, and we tell you those terms in writing before booking. For our own packages: 30 days or more before travel, the advance is refunded minus ₹1,000 per person; 15 – 29 days, 50% of the package; under 15 days, no refund. Date changes are free when the hotel allows.

faq.q: How much advance is needed and how do I pay?
faq.a: Tickets are paid in full at booking. For packages, 30% advance confirms the hotels and vehicle, and the balance is due 7 days before departure. UPI, bank transfer, card and cash at the office are all accepted, and you get a receipt and a GST invoice on WhatsApp.

faq.q: Do you help with visa, and how long does it take?
faq.a: Yes — we fill the form, check your documents, arrange the photo and book the appointment where one is needed. Dubai takes 4 – 5 working days, Thailand and Singapore about a week, Schengen 3 – 5 weeks including the appointment wait. The decision is the embassy's, so we advise applying well before booking non-refundable flights.

faq.q: Is the Char Dham yatra suitable for senior citizens?
faq.a: Many of our yatris are over 60. We keep the schedule gentle with an acclimatisation night, arrange pony, palki or helicopter for the Kedarnath climb at extra cost, and carry oxygen and first-aid in the vehicle. A doctor's fitness note is advised for anyone with heart or BP issues, and medical registration is compulsory on the route.

union.tagline: One voice for every shop in the market
union.about: We are the registered association of shopkeepers, wholesalers and small traders of the Sadar Bazar market area, run by a committee elected every two years by the members themselves. When a licence is held up, a GST notice lands, a road is dug up in front of your shop or a hawker encroachment blocks your shutter, the association takes it up with the Nagar Nigam, the police and the collectorate as one body instead of one lone shopkeeper. Members get a panel advocate, help with welfare-board and insurance forms, a WhatsApp notice group that reaches everyone within minutes, and a family support fund for the worst days. Every rupee of the membership fee is accounted for in the audited statement read out at the annual general body meeting.

offer.text: Enrol before Dhanteras and your member identity card and WhatsApp group addition are free with the first year's fee — bring your shop licence and two photos.

reviews.name: Mahesh G., cloth merchant
reviews.text: When the Nigam dug up the road in front of our lane for three weeks, the association got a written timeline and temporary planks for customers within two days. Alone I would still be making calls. Membership has paid for itself many times.

reviews.name: Sunita D., general store owner
reviews.text: I got a GST notice I could not understand. The help desk explained it, the panel advocate drafted the reply for ₹500 and it was closed without any penalty. The Tuesday sitting is worth it for every small shopkeeper.

reviews.name: Imran, mobile accessories shop
reviews.text: My cousin's shop caught fire last year and the support fund reached the family the same evening, before the insurance even started. That is when I understood why my father kept paying the yearly fee. The WhatsApp notices about power cuts and strikes are also very useful.

faq.q: Who can become a member?
faq.a: Any owner or registered tenant of a shop, godown, showroom or fixed stall within the market area covered by the association. Partners of one firm count as one membership; a second shop needs a second membership. Message us your shop address and we will confirm the same day.

faq.q: What is the membership fee and what does it cover?
faq.a: Annual membership is ₹1,200 per shop, valid April to March, and patron (lifetime) membership is ₹11,000. The fee covers grievance representation, the WhatsApp notice group, voting rights and member rates on the legal cell, help desk and hall. Fees are fixed by the general body and the audited statement is read out every year.

faq.q: How do I raise a complaint or problem?
faq.a: Send the issue on WhatsApp with photos and any paper you have (notice, bill, licence), or write it in the complaint register at the office. The secretary logs it with a number, the committee decides the action in its weekly sitting, and you get updates on the same WhatsApp thread till it is closed.

faq.q: Will the association fight my court case?
faq.a: The association does not fight personal cases, but the panel advocate reviews your papers for ₹500, drafts replies, and takes up your case at reduced fees if you choose. Matters affecting many members together, like a demolition notice for the whole lane, are taken up by the association in its own name.

faq.q: Is there any insurance or welfare benefit for members?
faq.a: Yes. Members can enrol in the group personal-accident cover for ₹450 a year during the April and October windows, and the family support fund gives immediate help in a fire, accident or death. We also help shop staff register with the labour welfare board for its scholarship and marriage assistance schemes.

faq.q: When are meetings held and how will I know?
faq.a: The executive committee sits every Wednesday evening at the office; the general body meets once a year in May and whenever an urgent issue needs it. Every notice, including bandh calls, power-cut schedules and Nigam drives, goes out on the members' WhatsApp group and on the notice board outside the office.

faq.q: Which purifier is right for my home, RO or UV?
faq.a: It depends on your water. Municipal supply below 300 TDS usually needs only UV + UF; borewell or tanker water above 300 TDS needs RO. We test your water free at home and suggest a model, and we will tell you if your existing purifier is enough.

faq.q: Do you give a demo of the alkaline ionizer before buying?
